title: Pizzazz
description: A small DOM-effects package with configurable click and hover bursts, CSS motion and explicit listener cleanup.
techStack: JavaScript, DOM, CSS transitions, Rollup, Jest
status: Legacy package; source reviewed at d265b1d. Current motion and icon-policy review remains open.

blocks.heading: A narrow animation API
blocks.body: Pizzazz attaches a click or hover effect to a DOM target. Options control the number and size of effect elements, duration, spread, rotation and easing. The package is independent of a UI framework and its reviewed package definition has no runtime dependencies.

blocks.heading: Motion comes from CSS transitions
blocks.body: A trigger creates a positioned container and span elements around the event location. Randomised target offsets give each burst variation. Rotation adds a transform; the gravity option chooses a downward target. CSS handles transform and opacity transitions, while timers start the movement and remove the container. Easing presets named bounce and spring are cubic-bezier values rather than a physical spring simulation.

blocks.heading: Give attachment a cleanup path
blocks.context: A reusable effect must stop listening when its target no longer belongs to an interface.

options.label: Attach a permanent global listener
options.detail: Every mount would leave another listener unless a caller managed it independently.

options.label: Return an unsubscribe function
options.detail: addPizzazz returns a function that removes the event handler it installed. Hover events can also be throttled.

blocks.outcome: A framework component can attach the effect and call its cleanup during unmount. Timed container removal handles the short-lived visual output separately from listener ownership.

blocks.heading: The implementation defines the next polish pass
blocks.body: The current presets are glyph-based, with a custom character option. Their presentation needs review against the current Lucide-only policy for owned sites, alongside reduced-motion behaviour, accessibility and repeated-trigger cleanup. The reviewed code does not establish a particle pool, a shared animation loop, a custom render callback or measured mobile frame-rate and bundle-size results. Those claims have been removed from the portfolio.

blocks.heading: Keep the example proportionate
blocks.body: This is a focused package API and lifecycle example. Rollup distribution and existing DOM-oriented tests are part of its source. It should be demonstrated with an actual recorded interaction and measured output before it is used as evidence of high-performance motion engineering.
